gap: No result ChatGPT got states that REDTIGER's own US store says the F77's SD card 'can only be used for video backup and transfer, not for direct recording', so the F77's built-in eMMC is all the loop space it has, or that DDPAI's own US store sells the Z90 Pro (64GB eMMC plus up to 512GB microSD, front + rear + cabin) for $199, $100 less than the $299 Z90 Master that ChatGPT showed.
standout_why: I compared against the cited 70mai.store M500 listing, the 70mai section of incartec, the incartec.co.uk M500 page (the same product as the cited incartec.com page, which failed its TLS check) and the manuals.plus M800 PDF. None of the 70mai pages says anything about the REDTIGER or DDPAI models. The incartec.co.uk M500 page gives one GBP price (£121.00) and no eMMC capacity. The manuals.plus PDF has no readable text. I could not open the cited shopredtiger.shop F77 page because its domain does not resolve, so I can't confirm it leaves out the SD-card limit. I also could not open the cited ddpai.com Z90 Master page (HTTP 429). As far as I could check, none of the cited pages gives the side-by-side US prices or the F77's no-recording-to-SD rule.
decides: For someone who wants built-in memory as well as front and rear coverage, the 70mai M800 at $159.99 is still the cheapest front-and-rear pick with 128GB eMMC. The F77 ($219.99) loses on storage: it can never record to more than its eMMC, because the SD slot only backs up and transfers. The Z90 Master ($299) loses to our DDPAI Z90 Pro ($199), which has the same 64GB eMMC, takes microSD up to 512GB, and covers three channels including 4G. The M500 ($69.99 and up) is only the pick for a front-only setup.
